name: English Separatism

facts.value: 1567-1571 pioneers. Separatist theory defined by Robert Browne 1580-1581

citations.excerpt: “Reformation without tarrying for Anie” was the burden laid on the heart of the Congregational pioneers in 1567–1571
and 1580–1581, when he first defined his Separatist theory.
and of the few cases in which these shaded off into practical Separatism
To this fact the very nickname “Brownists,” usually given to early “Separatists” by accident, but Congregationalists in essence, is itself witness.

facts.value: English Protestants who separated from the established church to form gathered congregations of committed believers bound by covenant.

citations.excerpt: It involved for him a definite "covenant" entered into by all members of the church, with God and with God's people, to abide by Christ's laws as ruling all their conduct, individually and collectively.
“The kingdom of God was not to be begun by whole parishes, but rather of the worthiest, were they never so few.”
“the first that made separation from the Reformed Church of England, having gathered congregations of their own.”
